text:
Arjun: RFC follow-up — thinking through the v1 -> v2 deprecation, wanted to surface a slightly different pattern: a "deprecation coordinator" service that owns short-lived shims and rollout signals. Thoughts?
Nate: Curious — what problem this solves that a gateway-side shim doesn't?
Arjun: Two main things: (1) lifecycle ownership (so eng teams don't manage long-lived sidecars), (2) unified telemetry and rollback hooks. The coordinator would create per-tenant HTTP proxies that translate v1 -> v2 at ingress and can be retired centrally.
Sophia: I like central ownership for telemetry, but worried about latency + memory on coordinator when we spin proxies for lots of tenants.
Kai: Agree with Sophia. Also need fail-open semantics — if coordinator flakes, we can't cause customer outages.
Arjun: Good call. Proposal: coordinator runs control plane only. It orchestrates lightweight sidecars (ephemeral, per-region) deployed to the same pool as edge proxies. Sidecars do the fast path translation locally; coordinator handles rollout, telemetry aggregation, and kill-switch.
Nate: So coordinator != data plane. Sidecars are still data-plane but created/removed by coordinator. That mitigates latency concerns.
Sophia: How will we tag/route traffic to the sidecars? Header sniffing? tenant-id?
Kai: We already have tenant header X-RW-Tenant. Sidecars can register a prefix in the edge routing table via our edge registry. Coordinator writes to registry.
Arjun: Exactly. Registration flow: coordinator -> edge-registry API -> edge routing tables (atomic update). Edge proxies prefer sidecar routes if present. If sidecar down, fallback to v2.
infra-bot: deploybot: scheduled canary for coordinator service tomorrow 06:00 UTC (canary=5 nodes)
Nate: What about auth/ACL differences between v1 and v2 clients? Some v1 clients depend on header munging we removed in v2.
Sophia: Sidecar can do header compatibility transforms. But we should encourage clients to move to compliant auth — add a deprecation header in responses: `X-RW-Deprecation: v1 -> v2; fallback-ttl=30d`
Kai: Rollout plan thought: phased tenant cohorts (10%, 25%, 50%, 100%), but cohorts by risk profile + traffic pattern. Coordinator needs an API to opt a tenant into shim for testing.
Arjun: Yep — coordinator UI/APIs: opt-in, force-opt-out, telemetry stream for each tenant, and emergency global cutoff. Also expose an event log for audits.
Nate: Telemetry required: per-tenant error-rate, p50/p95 latency delta vs native v2, token-rate, 5xxs introduced by shim. Also sample request/response diffs for regressions.
Sophia: We should also capture model-output regression signals for LLM responses — the shim sometimes rewrites request shape that changes model behavior. We need prompt-set based checks.
Kai: Could route a 1% shadow copy of traffic to native v2 (no transform) and compare outputs asynchronously. Coordinator could synthesize regression alerts when diffs exceed thresholds.
Arjun: Exactly. Shadowing + deterministic eval prompts. If regression > threshold, coordinator auto-pauses rollout and notifies on-call.
Nate: How long is the grace period? We want to be strict but not break customers. Maybe default 90 days with per-tenant override?
Sophia: Make it configurable: org-level default 90 days, but opt-in shorter windows for security teams. Also emit telemetry to tenant owner email.
Kai: Operational constraints: sidecars will increase operational surface. Need auto-heal: if sidecar fails too often, coordinator marks tenant for forced migration and alerts SRE.
Arjun: For deprecation sunset, coordinator will start returning 410 + `Retry-After` after N days unless tenant opted-in extension. But we should also provide a CLI helper that scans code for v1 usage patterns and provides migration suggestions.
Nate: CLI + migration assistant + sample patch diffs would be huge. Could run static scans on repos reachable via orgs? Privacy concerns though.
Sophia: For compliance, scans should be opt-in and only run on repos customers allow. We can offer the assistant as a self-serve tool.
Kai: Security note: sidecars will have access to request payloads. We need RBAC and KMS boundaries; ensure sidecars run in customer VPCs for Private deployments.
Arjun: Agreed — model: hosted customers use Redwood-managed sidecars in our tenancy; Private deployments run coordinator control plane with customer-managed sidecars. RBAC enforced via service identity.
Nate: Any thought on long-term: we should avoid sidecars becoming permanent. Maybe auto-expire sidecars after X days unless tenant has a migration plan ticket.
Sophia: Auto-expiry + Slack/email nudges and a one-click extension to reduce churn. Also export telemetry to tenant S3 so they can own data.
Kai: Performance: include a small cache layer in sidecar for prefix/KV caching to reduce recomputation and reduce model calls when possible. But caches should be transparent and have eviction metrics.
Arjun: Good. Implementation checklist draft: 1) coordinator MVP (control APIs, registry hooks, telemetry stream), 2) edge sidecar binary (transform, cache, healthcheck), 3) rollout UI + CLI, 4) shadowing/eval harness, 5) security/KMS integration, 6) expiration + billing signals.
Nate: Can we keep sidecar simple by reusing existing edge-plugin runtime? Avoid duplicating engineering.
Arjun: Yes — plan is to extend the edge-plugin runtime with a compatibility mode and keep shim logic as a config-driven transform set.
Sophia: One more UX ask: when we send deprecation headers to clients, include a link to migration guide + estimated impact metrics. Helps PS and customers.
Kai: Sounds good. Also add a `deprecation_status` field to tenant metadata in control plane.
Arjun: I'll draft a follow-up RFC with the coordinator API shapes, edge registry contract, and the rollout matrix. Link to draft: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/dep-coordinator-draft (WIP). Please add comments on the API shapes section.
Nate: Will do. :thumbsup:
Sophia: I'll add the telemetry requirements to the metrics RFC.
Kai: I'll prototype the sidecar health/registry registration this week and ping infra-bot when ready.
infra-bot: note: triage created ticket INFRA-4721 for sidecar registration prototype
Arjun: Thanks team — nice alignment. If nobody objects, I'll spin the RFC and schedule a 30m sync to walk the architecture next Tue.
Nate: No objections from me.
Sophia: +1
Kai: +1
Arjun: tagging @oncall for visibility and @solutions for migration helper feedback.
